_source.items: drafter.item1 to item4, extracted programmatically, byte for byte

goal_is_the_aim: The goal carries the user's CURRENT governing aim and the target, if any, that actually belongs to it. Use the original brief together with verified retained corrections; explicit later framing supersedes earlier framing where they conflict. Preserve an eventual ambition separately from the current task and never infer that the largest or earliest number is the operative target. A date is not automatically the goal: preserve whether it is a deadline for achieving the aim, a launch or start reference, or a measurement or learning window. Use event_by_date only when delivering the stated event is itself an aim; do not replace a quantity goal with an unrelated event or move its governing target into constraints to do so. Further mandatory targets of the same purpose may stay as target constraints: preserve their AND meaning, common reference and window, and all limits and conditions. If the governing meaning is unclear, retain the original words and ask; do not invent a target or a launch-completion percentage.
date_not_asked: For an event-by-date model, the host supplies the deadline question; do not add that same question to unknowns. Ask only relevant remaining timing questions, such as how long the current team would take or when new capacity becomes effective, when those facts are genuinely missing.
unknowns_description: Questions people could answer, scientific uncertainties and competing interpretations relevant to the shared work, in plain words. Preserve retained questions and viewpoints with their complete wording, speakers, qualifications and unresolved status; do not turn them into established causal facts. Do not predict how the host will treat, admit, verify, record or count a figure: Olumi’s current readback states what is actually held.
goal_level_in_other_words: When the retained brief states today’s level of the same whole goal quantity in other words, at the same reference and scope, set goal.baseline_value to that level with baseline_known true and baseline_provenance explicit. Matching units or a figure alone is insufficient: a component’s output, another service’s level, a target, a ceiling or a future forecast is not today’s whole-goal level. A level derived through an existing supported definition must retain its validated operands and conditions and its derived or inferred origin, not become an explicitly measured figure. If the whole-goal equivalence is unsupported, missing or conflicting, keep the baseline unknown; do not borrow a component or assume a zero.
